So a few weeks ago, I was looking at my skill queue with an eye towards training towards T3Ds, and noticed that propulsion jamming 4 was there. So I said fuck it, and kicked it up to 5.

Now I'm a few hours away from interdictors, and my head is filled with thoughts of camping pipes, tackling supers, and cleverly ensnaring warping ships in ambushes between gates. In other words, I'm probably going to lose some Sabres.

So does anyone have any advice, tips, or tricks they'd like to share with a newbie dictor pilot?
Tips for a newbie interdictor pilot?

Get used to dieing if you're not already. dictors are great but fragile so they die alot, just the way it is. Try not to be too enthusiastic about dropping a bubble unless your FC needs it and calls for it. I've been in fleets with dictors that have been a little jumpy and bubbled the fleet then we were just sitting ducks for the enemies. And decide what kind of bubbler you're going to be. Do you want to be the guy that sits on a gate waiting for some poor chump to jump in and catch him in a bubble or are you going to be the hero dictor that stays ahead of the enemy fleet while they try to run and trapping them in place while your fleet destroys them. Good luck

You might want to consider training Thermodynamics V and Nanite Operation/Interfacing to IV or V if you're going to be a fleet dictor. You'll be overheating your prop mod frequently and they tend to burn out. Maybe keep one or two spares in your cargo hold. Have fun, they're awesome and a well placed bubble is a thing of beauty!
Grab an inty while you train. Go make drag spots at various distances from all gates in direction of other gates. Being able to pop a bubble and drag people off gate can be really useful.
